mappings.note: Names hormones as the chemicals that regulate growth and development: the mechanism of the process.
Names a government scheme supporting menstrual hygiene, which belongs with the sanitation-practice items.
Names a recommended physical activity: a health habit for daily life.
Names the voice box as the structure that grows in adolescent boys. Identification of a part; the item on why the voice deepens is on LO-69.
Defines adolescence and its age band, and says why the stage matters. Recognition of the stage, so LO-65 rather than LO-67, where the kinds of change are sorted.
Two physical changes in boys beyond height: observable changes recalled for one sex, with no comparison asked for.
Two physical changes in girls beyond height, the companion single-sex item.
Acne explained by increased oily secretion clogging pores: the visible change traced to its cause.
Defines the secondary sexual characteristics category and populates it with an example from each sex: a category and its members.
Puberty as the maturation process inside adolescence: a process defined, not a feature observed.
Describes the cycle and the bleeding phase within it, the reproductive process in brief.
Why menstruation myths must be dispelled: they cause fear, shame and isolation. Freedom from prejudice, so LO-80 rather than the hygiene items on LO-78.
Names two emotional or behavioural changes, mood swings and stronger feelings, as signs of the stage. Not LO-77, since no way of managing them is asked for.
Why a balanced diet matters during rapid growth: nutrition applied to daily eating.
Two iron-rich foods and why iron matters, a diet-planning item.
Personal and menstrual hygiene to prevent infection is the good-sanitation-practices strand.
Wrapping and binning used pads, justified by community health and cleanliness, sits on the same sanitation outcome and reaches the environmental side of it.
Two benefits of regular activity, for body and mind: health habits in daily life.
Defines cyberbullying with an example: conduct towards others, so the values outcome.
Why social media must be used responsibly, with respect and care for privacy: the same values strand from the positive side.
Why adolescents should refuse harmful substances, argued from addiction and health damage. The health case, so LO-77; the peer-pressure items sit on LO-80.
Explains what addictive means as a dependency that develops and is hard to break: a process described.
Asks what hormones do during adolescence, i.e. which changes they trigger and regulate, so the changes are tied to their cause. The item that defines hormones themselves is on LO-70.
Why differing timing and rate is normal: the answer exists to remove anxiety and comparison, which is the freedom-from-fear strand.

Five-mark description of the physical changes in both sexes across height, body shape, voice and hair, which sets boys and girls side by side throughout. Not LO-65, because the comparison is the structure of the answer.
Defines secondary sexual characteristics, says why they appear and lists three per sex: the category filled out in full.
Names the emotional and behavioural changes (LO-65) and then asks how an adolescent can manage them positively (LO-77). Both halves carry marks.
Nutritional needs of this stage (LO-77) together with the hygiene practices it calls for (LO-78). The question names both explicitly.
Explains menstruation as a natural process (LO-70) and then argues that the myths around it must be challenged (LO-80).
Health risks of substance abuse (LO-77) plus why adolescents are vulnerable to pressure and how to refuse (LO-80). The strategies half is squarely about standing firm.
Cyberbullying, responsible use and what to do if targeted: conduct and courage towards others throughout.
Explains what hormones are and how they travel and act to regulate the changes: the mechanism in full, so LO-70 rather than the cause-attribution item on LO-69.
Analyses why each person's pace is their own and why knowing that prevents anxiety and comparison: freedom from fear and from judging others.
Ties diet, hygiene, activity, emotions and social conduct together into a healthy adolescence: the whole chapter turned into everyday practice.
The advice to Sameer is that everyone develops at their own pace and he need not worry, which is reassurance against fear rather than a health measure.
What the school could do for students like Priya: disposal bins, pads and awareness, i.e. sanitation provision. Not LO-80, because the asked-for answer is facilities, not attitudes.
Which further habit of the better-eating friend helps health: another everyday health practice.
What Riya should prioritise when targeted online, not engaging, saving evidence, blocking and telling an adult: the values and safety strand.
Vikram must refuse the cigarette firmly despite his friends: standing up to peer pressure, so LO-80 rather than the health-reason items on LO-77.
